title: Decode an FP8 byte
goal:
Table 1 of the paper (Section 3) lists the bit layout of the two FP8 encodings. Write `decode(code, fmt)`, which turns an integer `code` in `0..255` into the float that the byte `S.E.M` encodes. `fmt` is `"e4m3"` or `"e5m2"`.

The starter gives the field widths and biases in `FORMATS`. Handle three cases: subnormals (exponent field 0), normals, and the special values. E5M2 follows IEEE 754 and uses the top exponent for infinities and NaNs. E4M3 has no infinities and keeps a single NaN pattern, `S.1111.111` (Section 3.1).
hints: Split the byte with shifts and masks: the sign is bit 7, the exponent is the next `ebits` bits, and the mantissa is the low `mbits` bits.
A normal value is $(-1)^S \cdot (1 + M / 2^m) \cdot 2^{E - \text{bias}}$. A subnormal value is $(-1)^S \cdot (M / 2^m) \cdot 2^{1 - \text{bias}}$. The subnormal exponent is `1 - bias`, not `-bias`.

For E4M3, only the pattern with exponent field 15 and mantissa 7 is NaN. The other patterns with exponent field 15 are ordinary numbers up to 448. For E5M2, exponent field 31 with mantissa 0 is infinity, and the other mantissas are NaN.
